I am a PhD student in Political Science at [American University](https://www.american.edu/spa/gov/) in Washington, DC, working in comparative politics and political methodology.

I study how climate shocks and the infrastructure that fails after them shape democratic accountability. When storms knock out power, when new data centers strain the grid, or when energy prices rise, who do voters hold responsible, and how do they respond at the ballot box? My work combines original geospatial data with causal inference designs, mostly in R, and spans Brazil, the United States, and Japan.

I also coordinate outreach for [CLIPPS](https://www.american.edu/spa/cep/), an NSF-funded expert survey of climate laws and institutions in roughly 80 countries.
